findings.reason: merge.js:27-32 now calls collection.constructor(iters[0]) for any empty collection. For Record({})(), toSeq().size is 0, and Record.js:56-57 builds a new RecordType, so the result is a different object. The locked test __tests__/issues.ts:135 expects emptyRecord.merge({id: 1}) toBe emptyRecord, so it fails. Kept at high because it breaks a locked acceptance test.
findings.claim: Removing the isRecord guard makes merge() on an empty Record return a new instance instead of the same one, which brings back the Issue #1785 regression.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `return isRecord(collection) ? collection // Record is empty and will not be updated: return the same instance : collection.constructor(iters[0]);` and replaces it with an unconditional `return collection.constructor(iters[0]);`. An empty Record such as `Record({})()` has `toSeq().size === 0`, so it reaches this branch. `RecordType` in src/Record.js:52-97 builds `new RecordType(values)` because `values` is not an instance of `RecordType`, so the result is a fresh object. The locked test at __tests__/issues.ts:135 expects `emptyRecord.merge({ id: 1 })` to be `emptyRecord` (`toBe`), and CHANGELOG.md:628 records this guard as the fix for #1785.

findings.reason: wrapIndex in TrieUtils.ts:54-58 turns a non-numeric index like undefined into NaN, and updateList in List.js:441 returns the list unchanged for NaN. Unknown keys are dropped safely, so the only real effect is the new instance already covered by C1/X1.
findings.claim: For an empty Record, keys the Record doesn't define reach the constructor and call l.set(undefined, v).
findings.evidence: In src/Record.js:93-94 the constructor runs `KeyedCollection(values).forEach((v, k) => { l.set(this._indices[k], ...) })`. For `Record({})`, `_indices` is `{}`, so `this._indices['id']` is `undefined` and the call becomes `l.set(undefined, 1)`. The removed guard avoided this by returning the existing instance.
